title: Scheduling your training for White Collar workers
summary: NH on programming for office workers. Recovery windows are wide, so they can train close to maximum recoverable volume, but they need to fight a sedentary lifestyle, poor posture and stress. He recommends walking and calisthenics, says to keep the gym from becoming a second job, and suggests 4-6 sessions a week on upper/lower, gentleman or push/pull/legs splits.
claims: Office workers sit 7-8 hours a day and are very sedentary compared with blue-collar workers, who have to manage physical volume coming from work
A white-collar job is the best job for focusing on powerlifting or bodybuilding because all your physical energy can go to training
Sitting with rounded shoulders all day can carry over into lifting form, such as pulling and squatting with a rounded spine, and lead to injuries; fix posture
Mental stress from work can ruin focus and weight selection and aggravate injuries, especially tendinitis, especially when it costs you sleep; you are never at 100%
Training can relieve work stress so you go home to family life without that negative energy
Sedentary workers should add walking, steps, a stepper or laps, and calisthenics like pull-ups and push-ups to keep the ability to move the body through space
NH stopped vertical pulls for a long time and was terrible when he returned because the neurological adaptation was gone
If you cannot get to the gym, bring a pull-up bar to work and do pull-ups and push-ups there
Office workers have excellent recovery windows because work is not physically stressful, as long as they eat enough
Office workers can always aim for maximum recoverable volume because nothing outside the gym will raise the pot's level; blue-collar workers need to stay lower in case work gets physical
Being a professional who only trains is best, but a white-collar job is the second-best situation for building muscle
Athletes training on the side also get volume from other sources and must account for it
Office workers can specialise more freely than soldiers, who need to run and climb, but should keep a fun side pursuit so they are not trapped if their love for one practice dies
Do not let the gym become a second job; keep the time after work free even though you have the recovery to make training very serious
Blue-collar workers should train shorter, more minimal and more intense sessions with recovery windows before heavy work days
White-collar workers can benefit from training 4 to 6 times a week; upper/lower, gentleman splits or push/pull/legs twice a week all work well
